articles.title: Denticle Armor
articles.summary: Pointed plates with split keels, root collars and worn patches, separated by between-plate pores; directional rough shine. Clearly horizontal-banded sawtooth texture, like corrugated or scaled metal; the rows stay visible longer than the individual points.
articles.what: Pointed plates carry split keels, root collars, worn patches and separate between-plate pores. Up close: Strict horizontal rows, each 28-30 px tall and separated by dark lines, filled with small pointed triangles, like roof tiles or shark denticles, with a tiny dot between every pair. Triangle peaks glow in the highlight; stronger and more even on metallic. From a distance: Clearly horizontal-banded sawtooth texture, like corrugated or scaled metal; the rows stay visible longer than the individual points. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Skin & Cellular (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Skin & Cellular", or search for "Denticle Armor".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Sides and rocker where horizontal rows suit the body line
Bumpers and hood; rows fight vertical stripes
Rows are strong; numbers need bold weight and a contrasting colour.
Clear row-by-row triangle scales in the highlight, strong banding
Pairs well with: matte, metallic, gloss, chrome.
pitfalls: Not a shark skin paint pattern: it adds no colour
Not brushed metal: it has pointed scales in rows, not smooth streaks
Avoid: strong directionality on curved panels, too busy under stripes.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Denticle Armor over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Diatom Sieve
articles.summary: Dense pore-row sieve bands, bilateral ribs and rims; matte micro-relief, almost no specular pop. A regular perforated-metal or speaker-grille look; the ovals blend into a fine even mesh texture.
articles.what: Bilateral pennate frustules contain an axial raphe, repeated pore rows, terminal plugs and separate valve rims. Up close: A neat staggered field of upright oval pods, about 20 x 28 px, each a dark oval with a lighter centre seam and tiny rib marks, like a perforated sheet or a field of seeds. On metallic the ovals read as clean dark holes in a bright plate. From a distance: A regular perforated-metal or speaker-grille look; the ovals blend into a fine even mesh texture. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Skin & Cellular (Surface library tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, sides, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Surface library tab and the group "Skin & Cellular", or search for "Diatom Sieve".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, sides and under stripes for a mesh or grille feel
Flat panels where the oval grid stays regular
Moderate texture; bold numbers stay readable.
Visible oval grid with softer, lower contrast
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not a mesh paint pattern: it adds no black holes of paint
Not carbon weave: shapes are ovals, not threads
Avoid: kills gloss highlights, very busy up close.
